content: If you experience any of the following symptoms, it is important to seek medical attention promptly: 1. Persistent watery diarrhea or diarrhea that does not resolve. 2. Blood present in your stool. 3. Severe abdominal cramps. 4. Fever that begins after starting or stopping the medication. 5. Severe skin reactions. Rabeprazole has the potential to cause serious skin reactions, including Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), which can be life-threatening if untreated. If you develop a rash, discontinue rabeprazole immediately and contact your healthcare provider. Seek emergency medical help if you experience symptoms of SJS or TEN, such as: Painful red or purple skin that appears burned and peels. Flat red rashes or blisters on the skin, mouth, nose, or genitals. Red, painful, watery eyes. Rabeprazole can also cause a severe allergic reaction known as DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms), which may affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms of DRESS include: Skin rash or hives. Fever or a general feeling of being unwell. Swollen lymph nodes. Shortness of breath. Swelling in the feet, ankles, or legs. Dark-colored urine. Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Rabeprazole may trigger or worsen lupus, an autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues. Notify your healthcare provider if you develop new or worsening joint pain or a rash on your arms or cheeks. Long-term use of rabeprazole (three years or more) may lead to vitamin B-12 deficiency. Symptoms of low vitamin B-12 levels include: Sore tongue. Weakness. Tingling or numbness in the hands or feet. Rabeprazole can also cause hypomagnesemia (low magnesium levels), which can result in serious complications such as seizures or heart rhythm problems. Symptoms of hypomagnesemia include: Changes in heart rate or rhythm, such as a fast or irregular heartbeat. Dizziness. Muscle spasms. Seizures. Prolonged use of rabeprazole, especially in older adults or at high doses, may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures. Rabeprazole may cause severe allergic reactions. Discontinue use and seek immediate medical attention if you experience: Breathing difficulties or wheezing. Rapid heartbeat. Fever or general malaise. Swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat. Difficulty swallowing or throat tightness. Itching, rash, or hives. Nausea or vomiting. Dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting. Stomach cramps. Joint pain. Precautions: Do not use rabeprazole if you are allergic to it, other proton pump inhibitors, or any of its ingredients. Consult your pharmacist for a complete list of ingredients. Inform your healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking to avoid potential drug interactions. Rabeprazole should only be taken as prescribed by a healthcare provider. Do not share it with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Do not chew, cut, or crush rabeprazole tablets. Antacids may be used alongside rabeprazole if needed. Rabeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to take full effect. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: The effects of rabeprazole on pregnancy and breastfeeding are not well understood. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Rabeprazole may interact with certain medications, including methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, tacrolimus, and some antiretroviral drugs. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications you are taking. Overdose: In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take double doses.
